findings.quote: [P1] Isolate client certificates from the shared context — `src/requests/adapters.py:94-95`. Every default-verified request receives the same module-level SSLContext, including requests with different `cert` values and requests with no client certificate. urllib3's `ssl_wrap_socket` calls `load_cert_chain` on that supplied context when a certificate is provided, and never removes it. Consequently, after one mTLS request, later connections from any session can present that identity to a different server that requests a client certificate, even if the later request did not specify one. Concurrent requests with different certificates can also use the wrong identity. Pool keys distinguish the certificate paths, but the context behind those pools is still shared process-wide.

[P1] Keep adapter-specific CA certificates out of the global trust store — `src/requests/adapters.py:94-95`. A custom HTTPAdapter can configure `ca_certs` or `ca_cert_dir` on its PoolManager; urllib3 merges those settings with the request's `ssl_context` and calls `load_verify_locations` on that context when connecting. Since this change supplies the same context to every default-verified pool, a connection through that adapter permanently adds its private CA to the trust store used by unrelated sessions and hosts. A later ordinary request can therefore accept a certificate issued by that private CA, expanding trust beyond the adapter that configured it.

[P1] Preserve TLS configuration supplied by custom adapters — `src/requests/adapters.py:94-95`. The per-request `ssl_context` overrides an `ssl_context` configured by a subclass in `init_poolmanager`, because urllib3 merges request pool kwargs over the manager's defaults. It also causes urllib3 to skip constructing a context from manager settings such as `ssl_version` or `ssl_minimum_version`. Thus default-verified requests silently ignore custom trust, cipher, and protocol restrictions; for example, an adapter requiring TLS 1.3 can negotiate TLS 1.2 instead. The documented transport adapter pattern relies on those pool settings.

[P2] Avoid making the default CA bundle a prerequisite for importing Requests — `src/requests/adapters.py:75-78`. This runs context creation and CA loading while `requests` is imported, before any request or environment CA-bundle override is selected. If the default bundle is missing, unreadable, or invalid, importing Requests now fails even for HTTP-only use, `verify=False`, or applications that set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to a valid alternative. Previously the default bundle was accessed only when a default-verified HTTPS request was made. Similarly, Python installations without an SSL module can no longer import Requests for HTTP because `create_urllib3_context()` fails at import time.

[P2] Reload the default trust store when its bundle changes — `src/requests/adapters.py:75-78`. The module-level context reads the default bundle once and every later `verify=True` request reuses it. Previously each new TLS connection loaded the bundle path, so replacing a bundle in a long-running process affected new connections. After this change, newly added roots remain unusable and removed or compromised roots remain trusted until the process restarts, even after existing connection pools are closed.
